issues.what: Rationale says "The ASR transcript (E11) confirms the speaker claims to show 'living worms' in Lipton tea", but the ASR observation at turn 1 showed only backend metadata and limitations, with no transcript text. The quote 'living worms' first becomes visible only after E11 is read in full at turn 10.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches the student to quote and cite the contents of a record it has not seen, which is hallucination with a citation attached.
issues.ideal: Say the ASR result E11 is ready but its text has not been read yet, and justify OCR by the on-screen packaging visible in E3/E5/E8/E10.

issues.what: The answer says ABC News reports Lipton "demonstrated that its lemon pieces dissolve in hot water" [E20]. That detail is not in the W1-1 report (F1 only says Lipton identified them as lemon pieces), GIA never read E20, and the visible part of E20 does not contain it.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: The coordinator adds a factual detail that appears nowhere in its State (the report, plus its one READ_RECORD of E15), so the student learns to enrich answers from outside knowledge.
issues.ideal: Restrict the answer to what the W1-1 findings state, or have the worker put the dissolving demonstration in its report with an E20 citation first.

issues.what: The worker read three news pages that all repeat the same Lipton Facebook statement (E20, E21, E22) but never opened R4 thatsnonsense.com (E23), the only fact-check-style source in the results. The report and answer then hedge: "not independent laboratory identification", "composition was not independently verified".
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches reading redundant copies of one company statement instead of the source most likely to give independent analysis, and then reporting the gap as unresolved.
issues.ideal: After E20, read E23 (and/or search for an independent test, e.g. dissolving the pieces in hot water) instead of a third outlet repeating the company statement.

issues.what: Rationale: "Read E22 (Metro) to obtain the specific date of Lipton's Facebook statement". No date from E22 is ever used in the report, and the read only corroborates what E20/E21 already said.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It gives a stated purpose for the read that is never followed through, which makes a redundant read look justified.
issues.ideal: Skip E22, or if it is read, use the date it gives in the report.

issues.what: get_frames at 41.51 s and 124.53 s returned E5 and E9 again, frames that were already in the materials. The rationale is generic ("evenly spaced times ... verify whether worm-like objects appear throughout"), and no denser sampling was done to check the movement that the report later says it cannot establish.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It re-extracts known frames instead of targeting the question the claim hinges on, which is whether the pieces move.
issues.ideal: Extract closely spaced frames (e.g. 1 s apart) in the span where pale pieces appear (~69-97 s) to test for independent movement.

issues.what: T1 copies the overall task verbatim ("Fact-check the following claim, which circulated as the title...") with no decomposition, e.g. separate points for what the video shows, whether the pieces move, and what Lipton and independent sources say.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches copying the task through instead of planning which sub-questions must be answered.
issues.ideal: Keep one workspace but list the sub-questions in its Scope: speaker's claim (ASR), visual check for movement, the company response, and an independent debunk.

issues.what: GIA reads E15 ("cited by the report but not attached; view it before answering") but then never uses or cites E15. The 'revised' answer after the verifier's sloppy_numeric/major flag is word-for-word identical to the original. The closing limitation sentence pads citations: "[E16][E20][E21][E22]".
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches a ritual review step with no effect, and citation padding on a sentence that is a scope statement.
issues.ideal: Either use E15 in the answer or skip the read, and leave the scope or limitation sentence uncited or cite only what supports it.

good_patterns: Before reporting, the worker reads the full ASR transcript (turn 10) instead of relying on the truncated summary, and quotes the speaker's claim from it in F2.

Attribution stays accurate: the Lipton explanation is attributed to the company via news reports ("These reports support attributing the lemon-piece explanation to the company") and is not stated as established fact.
The visual findings are honest about what stills can show ("do not demonstrate independent movement ... Appearance alone does not establish that the pieces are lemon ingredients either").
After a failed search, the next query is reformulated with a reason ("video" -> "hoax") rather than repeated verbatim.
cannot_judge: Whether the F2 quotes and details ("worms inside, living worms", expiry 2017, four or five packs) match E11; the transcript is truncated (+4284 chars).
Whether the 'dissolve in hot water' detail is present in the full E20 text (truncated +808 chars); even if it is, it was not in GIA's visible State.

Whether the frame descriptions in F3 (pale yellow curved pieces at 69.167/96.875 s, box at 152.208 s) and the turn 3 claim that E3/E5/E8/E10 'do not clearly show any worms' match the images, since the images are not rendered.
What the verifier's sloppy_numeric/major issue referred to, since the revision changed nothing.
summary: This is a short, mostly sound video fact-check: ASR, OCR, a structure pass and frames, then one productive search with three news reads, a full transcript review and a carefully hedged report and answer that attributes the 'lemon pieces' explanation to Lipton. The serious problems are two hidden-knowledge leaks. The turn 2 rationale quotes 'living worms' from a transcript that had not been read yet, and the final answer adds the 'dissolve in hot water' demonstration, which does not appear in any report GIA saw. Lesser problems: three reads of the same company statement while the fact-check site E23 was skipped, re-extracting existing frames instead of testing for movement, a verbatim task copy in the plan, and a review read plus answer revision that change nothing.
